planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in an open, fast-draining orchid bark mix; this 1950 Bow Bells x mossiae cross carries huge, ruffled white flowers with a deep magenta throat and remains one of the most award-decorated cattleya hybrids ever registered.

directions: Pot in coarse fir bark or a similar chunky orchid mix that drains within seconds of watering, since the thick roots rot quickly if kept soggy. Provide bright, filtered light such as an east window or shaded lath house, with morning sun and afternoon shade being ideal. Water thoroughly when the mix approaches dryness and feed at quarter to half strength with a balanced fertilizer during active growth, tapering back once new pseudobulbs mature. Expect large, fragrant white blooms with a vivid magenta lip once mature canes finish maturing, typically in spring.
sources: American Orchid Society - Orchids Magazine cattleya hybrid history

common_name: Sarah Jean Ice Cascade Cymbidium (Pendulous Cascading Orchid)

planting.note: Grow in a hanging basket or elevated container in bright, indirect light so the pendant flower spikes can trail freely; this pumilum x Sleeping Beauty cross needs a cool autumn night drop to trigger its cascading, scented white sprays.

directions: Plant in a hanging basket or raised pot filled with a fine bark and sphagnum mix so the pendulous flower spikes can drape over the rim unobstructed. Give bright, filtered light year-round and, in late summer and fall, allow nighttime temperatures to drop into the 50s Fahrenheit to encourage bud initiation. Water regularly through the growing season, letting the mix dry slightly between soakings, and reduce moisture once spikes appear so they do not rot. Long-lasting, fragrant white blooms cascade from the mature clumps in winter and are prized for cutting and hanging display.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society plant profile - Cymbidium Sarah Jean gx 'Ice Cascade'
Santa Barbara International Orchid Show class notes on pendulous cymbidiums

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in bright, indirect light in a small, free-draining pot; this 1973 Shiranami x Pinocchio nobile-type hybrid needs a cool, dry winter rest to set the dense clusters of white-and-magenta blooms along its canes.

directions: Pot in a small, well-drained container with fine bark or a bark-sphagnum blend, since nobile types prefer to be slightly pot-bound. Give bright, indirect light and regular water with fertilizer during the warm growing season while new canes lengthen. From autumn onward, cut back sharply on water and stop feeding while keeping the plant cool to trigger flower buds along the leafless canes instead of new plantlets. Resume watering as flower buds swell in late winter and enjoy the dense sprays of white blooms edged in rosy magenta.
sources: New York Botanical Garden research guide - Nobile Dendrobium Hybrids

common_name: Golden Elf Cymbidium (Miniature Fragrant Yellow Orchid)

planting.note: Grow as a compact houseplant or shaded patio container in bright, indirect light in a fast-draining bark mix; this 1978 Cym. ensifolium x Cym. Enid Haupt cross stays oncidium-sized and needs no cold winter dip to rebloom.

directions: Plant in a compact pot of medium-grade bark mix, since this hybrid stays far smaller than standard cymbidiums and does not need repotting often. Provide bright, filtered light such as a sheltered patio or bright windowsill, and unlike many cymbidiums it flowers reliably without a pronounced cool autumn snap. Water evenly through the growing season and feed lightly, easing back slightly once flower spikes emerge to prolong bloom. Clusters of small, intensely fragrant golden-yellow flowers appear from summer into winter on well-grown plants.
sources: Orchids.org grex database - Cymbidium Golden Elf
